title: perf(firmware): bound retained diagnostic descriptions
body:
## Summary

Reduce temporary diagnostic allocations when inspecting large UF2 and DfuSe files. The decoders now construct only the four descriptions that their existing summaries display, while counting every omitted description. All payload regions, metadata, coverage, integrity facts and summary wording remain unchanged.

## Problem and expected behavior

At base `d5a942177fad030d3caf0f8d39856c116e3e5cda`, `overlappingElements` formats a string for each nonempty overlapping DfuSe element; `numberingFacts` similarly retains every absent or ambiguous UF2 numbering-group description. Their consumers later display only four examples. Thus an admitted file can allocate tens of thousands of strings that are immediately discarded.

Related: #8230 / `1f935949ff904165f90b4740eb283a8218275a13` bounded descriptions for **empty** DfuSe declarations during the target walk. This change covers retained nonempty payload overlaps and UF2 numbering groups, which that patch and its review discussion left unchanged. #11296 centralized summary formatting with `boundedList`; it did not bound these producers. No separate issue is linked because the reproduction, measurements and proposed repair are included here.

## Change and scope

The two domain producers return `BoundedList<string>` with explicit omitted counts. They still examine every element/group; only descriptions beyond the displayed four are avoided. UF2 formats group labels only when a retained description needs them. The existing consumers use the bounded owner for both wording and total counts. Both formats are included as one diagnostic-retention improvement.

## Contract and boundary impact

- Semantic owners: DfuSe overlap reporting and UF2 numbering facts; their artifact readers and CLI/MCP consumers retain the same facts.
- Contribution scope: ordinary optimization of existing local-file parsers; no advance scope decision required.
- CLI/MCP, provider and format compatibility: no input, output schema, ceiling or admission change.
- Evidence/provenance: entry identity, source ranges, payload bytes, coverage and integrity remain intact.
- Target authority and cleanup: unchanged file reads and existing reader lifetime.
- Generated metadata, packaging and installation: no changes.

Expected effects:

- [x] Read existing files or captured data.
- [ ] Launch or attach to a process.
- [ ] Inject instrumentation or run scripts/code.
- [ ] Change process memory, registers, files, or configuration.
- [ ] Contact network services.
- [ ] Recover protected code or work around protections.
- [ ] Documentation or usability only; no target interaction.
- [ ] Not sure yet; investigation or maintainer guidance needed.

## Evidence and regression coverage

- DfuSe regression retains the full element list and payloads while checking address-order descriptions, total overlap count, different alternate settings and the exact omitted count.
- UF2 regression combines nine groups with absent and ambiguous numbering, checks the two summaries in encounter order, every region's source block indices and all payload bytes, plus a complete group.
- These are semantic-preservation tests and pass on both implementations. The allocation change is established separately by native measurements, not by a claimed failing functional regression.

Measured using fresh Node 24.22.1 processes on Ubuntu 24.04, three alternating before/after rounds. Peak RSS includes the whole process through complete enumeration and JSON serialization. The public-reader tasks enumerate every entry; small tasks also open every payload stream. Large decoder tasks independently verify every payload byte. Full outputs are compared byte-for-byte.

| Completed public-reader task | Input | Peak RSS before | Peak RSS after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DfuSe, 65,536 nonempty overlapping elements | 786,733 bytes | 397,800 KiB | 360,460 KiB |
| UF2, 21,845 ambiguous numbering groups | 33,553,920 bytes | 282,844 KiB | 270,560 KiB |
| UF2, 65,536 absent-number groups | 33,554,432 bytes | 456,108 KiB | 456,260 KiB |
| UF2, 8,192 complete groups (control) | 8,388,608 bytes | 182,876 KiB | 185,832 KiB |

The first two tasks save median 36.46 MiB and 12.00 MiB respectively. The absence-only public task is essentially unchanged; the complete-group control increases by 2.89 MiB. Decoder-only peaks and all individual measurements are retained with the logs. Full output sizes are unchanged, including the 29,515,333-byte DfuSe inventory and 9,823,589-byte ambiguous UF2 inventory.

Small and non-overlapping cases show no meaningful memory improvement. These synthetic cases establish the reported memory effect; they do not establish a general CPU, latency or token reduction. No hardware flashing or third-party firmware corpus was used.

For evidence-bearing changes:

- [x] Observed, derived, and inferred claims remain distinguishable.
- [x] Artifact identity, source provenance, and failed attempts remain preserved.
- [x] Unsupported, incomplete, unavailable, or uncertain outcomes remain visible.

## Validation performed

At the pinned base plus the exact four files in this PR:

- `npm run test:local -- src/domain/firmware/dfuse.test.ts src/artifacts/DfuSeArtifactReader.test.ts src/domain/firmware/uf2.test.ts src/artifacts/Uf2ArtifactReader.test.ts` — **45 passed before and after**.
- `npm run test:focused -- tests/acceptance/firmwareContainersCli.test.ts tests/boundary/mcp/firmwareContainersMcp.test.ts` — **7 passed** with the combined change; the same seven passed on the baseline in the earlier run.
- `npm run check` — **passed**, including typecheck, lint, formatting, Knip, metadata and architecture checks; existing typed-lint advisory warnings remain.
- `git diff --check` — passed; the only source-worktree changes are the four PR files.
- **96 fresh native processes** across the DfuSe and UF2 probes: all completed, every full before/after output matched byte-for-byte. Independent assertions checked counts, ordering, addresses, coverage and payloads.
- [DfuSe native/public validation and original comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/rea/actions/runs/44032525389) and [combined exact-file validation, UF2 public measurements and full-history audit](https://github.com/Afloat16/rea/actions/runs/44034092158) — successful. The latter records SHA-256 for all four tested files; production readback matches those bytes.

The earlier validation workflow initially failed to start because of a job-level context expression; the corrected workflow completed. No failed or interrupted run is counted as a pass.

## Compatibility, safety, and release

No breaking change, migration, dependency or package change. Validation covers native Node/Linux parsers, the production ArtifactReader APIs, and the compiled CLI/MCP firmware tests; no Hopper/Ghidra or browser provider is involved. Existing parser and reader regressions remain in the selected suites. No new execution or mutation capability is introduced.

## Author readiness

Human owner: @Afloat16

- [ ] I reviewed the final diff and relevant existing code, understand the change and its edge cases, and take responsibility for the complete PR, including AI-assisted work.
- [ ] I checked the evidence above, confirmed it supports the current change, and recorded meaningful validation gaps.
- [ ] I declare this PR ready for initial maintainer review.

## Before merge

- [x] This PR addresses a concrete problem or an agreed enhancement.
- [x] Material scope and authority questions are resolved, and any required maintainer scope decision covers the final diff.
- [x] The PR has one focused outcome and the title follows `type(scope): outcome`.
- [x] Related issue is linked, or the reason for not linking one is stated above.
- [x] Tests cover changed observable behavior and meaningful failure paths.
- [x] Owning docs, contracts, and generated metadata are updated where needed.
- [x] User-visible CLI/MCP changes include representative output.
- [x] I checked the final diff for secrets, unrelated cleanup, and unsupported claims.
